key: Ye are the children of the LORD your God: ye shall not cut yourselves, nor make any baldness between your eyes for the dead.
s: Moses opens a chapter of laws that moves from mourning customs to clean food and the tithe; Rashi, on 14:1, reads it as children of God keeping themselves comely, not gashed or made bald, and Ibn Ezra, on 14:1, as children trusting a loving Father whose every deed is for good, though beyond their understanding.

evidence.gloss: [Rashi on 14:1, ‘ye shall not cut yourselves’:] because you are children of the Omnipresent, and it is fitting for you to be comely, not gashed and made bald … [Ibn Ezra on 14:1, ‘and the sense of children’:] once you know that you are children to God, and He loves you more than a father loves his son, do not gash yourselves over anything He does, for all that He does is for good; and if you do not understand it, as little children do not understand their father’s deeds but simply rely on him.
